raw.assessment: The incumbent provides a rendered combination and accessible history, both useful for checking embedded captions and retaining delivered work. It achieved the timing target in 20/30 sampled sessions, below the required 27/30. Four downloads had unexpected captions; one also had an unexpected video cut. These observations do not distinguish incorrect render inputs from selection of an otherwise correctly rendered older pair. Completion-order reversals and inconsistent pairing records make identity confusion plausible, not established. H1-O7 limits any claim that full rendering necessarily prevents timely, confident previews: nine single-correction sessions succeeded in five to 11 minutes. Its relationship to the longer sessions remains unmeasured.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: bind each render request to immutable video and caption snapshots, show that pair beside its result, and verify worker input hashes against the request before making it downloadable.
openings.delta: Makes intended input identity inspectable independently of completion order and distinguishes wrong-input production from wrong-result selection.
openings.prediction: Under deliberately reversed completion order, downloadable results match their recorded input pair, and editors more reliably select the pair they explicitly intended.
openings.probe: On private staging with fabricated footage, change both caption and video versions between overlapping requests. Compare request, worker and output identities; ask both editors to select the intended result. Include retrieval of the last delivered wording. Reject mismatched results.
assumptions: Snapshot binding and verification fit four engineer-days and current processing allowance; this requires a scoped estimate.
The recorded intended pair is confirmed by the editor.
Delivered snapshots remain retained on existing private accounts.

openings.claim: Do repeated-edit sessions lose most time before the intended render becomes available, or afterward while identifying and reviewing it?
openings.delta: Determines whether reducing redundant render demand or improving result identification is the more relevant next intervention.
openings.prediction: A waiting account predicts predominantly pre-availability delay; an identification account predicts substantial post-availability delay. Single-correction sessions provide the supplied limiting comparison.
openings.probe: Combine render timestamps with brief staged editor observations recording final edit, intended-result availability, selection and successful review. Compare single versus repeated corrections within the one editor-day budget.
assumptions: Existing events identify requests sufficiently for timing attribution.
Staging results guide prioritization but do not establish festival capacity or the 30-session success measure.

raw.assessment: The stipulated observations show missed timing targets and unexpected source versions, but do not establish whether delays mainly arise from rendering or identifying previews. Neither opening establishes the success target without prospective testing.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: binding each render request to an immutable video-and-caption pair, and displaying that same pair identity throughout request, completion and download, reduces unexpected-version downloads despite completion reordering.
openings.delta: Replace reconstruction from editor filenames and completion numbers with one persistent pair record; retain the last delivered pair, original captions and video.
openings.prediction: Under deliberately reordered completions, editors choose their intended pair more reliably, and downloaded content hashes match its recorded inputs.
openings.probe: Use fabricated footage in private staging, two video cuts and multiple caption revisions. Have both editors select specified pairs under reordered completion, comparing the existing history with the proposed identity display. Verify downloaded content against the requested pair and verify continued access to the delivered wording.
assumptions: Immutable source references can be implemented within the shared four engineer-day budget.
Editors can recognize their intended pair from the displayed identity.

openings.claim: Rendering only when an editor explicitly requests a preview, while saving caption edits immediately, may reduce unnecessary work and waiting without reducing usable preview access.
openings.delta: Separate saving text from requesting a full embedded-caption preview; retain existing completed previews and the delivered version.
openings.prediction: Render count falls, but final-edit-to-correct-preview time improves only if avoidable renders contribute substantial queue time; extra request friction could instead worsen it.
openings.probe: Replay timestamped events to estimate avoidable processing, then compare save-triggered and explicit-request workflows in private staging. Measure queue, render, identification and viewing time separately; check whether either editor forgets to request a preview. Bound this trial within the shared editor-day and computing allowance.
assumptions: Editors accept an explicit preview action.
Implementation and both probes fit the shared resource budget.
Sampled-week demand cannot establish festival performance.

openings.claim: Bind renders to immutable video/caption pairs; display identity through request, completion and download; verify worker inputs before release and reject mismatches.
openings.discriminator: Wrong-input production versus wrong-result selection, independently of completion order.
openings.fit: Conditional: private accounts, embedded delivery and retained delivered pair/original wording; scope against four engineer-days, one editor-day and 80 processing hours/week.
openings.probe: Both editors compare existing/proposed displays on fabricated footage with overlapping revisions and reversed completions. Check request, worker and download identities, intended-pair selection and delivered-wording retrieval.
openings.uncertainty: Pair intention must be confirmed and recognizable; implementation cost and causal account remain unproved.

openings.claim: Determine whether repeated-edit delay precedes intended-result availability or follows it during identification/review.
openings.discriminator: Pre-availability delay favors demand reduction; post-availability delay favors identification changes.
openings.fit: Preserves constraints; share the one editor-day budget.
openings.probe: Join render timestamps to staged observations of final edit, availability, selection and successful review; compare single/repeated corrections.
openings.uncertainty: Events may not support attribution. Nine successful single-correction sessions limit claims against rendering.

openings.claim: Save captions immediately; render only on explicit preview request while retaining completed previews and delivered versions.
openings.discriminator: Fewer renders improve latency only if avoidable work causes queue delay; request friction may worsen it.
openings.fit: Private staging and embedded output preserve constraints; shared implementation, editor and compute budgets need confirmation.
openings.probe: Replay events for avoidable processing; compare automatic/explicit requests, measuring queue, render, identification and viewing times plus forgotten requests.
openings.uncertainty: Editor acceptance and festival demand remain unknown.

lineage.reason: With Z1; preserves continuous identity and selection comparison.

post_distill.decision: Probe identity and delay attribution before prioritizing demand reduction. Synthetic observations and staging establish neither festival capacity nor success: prospectively test 30 new sessions for at least 27 correctly identified previews within 15 minutes and zero unintended delivered pairings.
